Before you start

A simple plan you stick to is worth more than a perfect plan that stays in a drawer.

Most people don't fail in the markets for lack of information. There are videos, books and courses enough for several lifetimes. They fail for lack of a simple, written plan they can actually follow on a tired Tuesday, after work, with the phone ringing.

This guide is that plan. It has three steps, in order:

  1. Educate. Understand the game before risking a single euro.
  2. Create income. Choose the way of taking part in the market that fits your life.
  3. Automate. Put rules and tools to work for you, so you don't depend on willpower.
Key idea

Golden rule of this guide: don't move on to the next step before completing the previous one. Skipping steps is building the roof before the walls.

Who it's for

It's for people who have already realised they want to put their money to work and don't know where to begin. You don't need experience. You need fifteen minutes a day, a pen and the willingness to be honest with yourself on the worksheets.

If you don't yet have an emergency fund, or you have expensive debts, start with the other guide in this collection, "The First Step". This plan assumes that part is already sorted.

How to use this guide

Each step has two chapters. The first explains, the second gets you doing. The worksheets are inside the text: write on them, even if you're reading the PDF, or copy them into a notebook. A written plan gets carried out. A plan in your head gets bargained with every day.

I'm Ricardo Garcia, founder of MoreThanMoney. I spent fourteen years in uniform before I got into the markets, and I lost my first account by doing exactly the opposite of what's written here. This plan is what I wish I'd had on day one.

1

Step 1 · What you really need to know

You don't have to know everything. You have to know enough not to hurt yourself.

Miguel, 41, a sales rep in Leiria, opened his first broker account on a Saturday night. By Sunday he'd watched six videos. On Monday he opened three gold trades, at the maximum leverage the broker allowed. By Wednesday the account was half its value. He knew many things. He didn't know the four that matter.

The four ideas that separate those who last from those who disappear

Why 1% is so much

It sounds small. Risking 1% of a 1,000 € account means risking 10 € per trade. But look at what happens when you lose a lot in one go.

Someone who loses half their account needs to double what's left just to get back to the start. Someone who risks 1% can get it wrong ten times in a row and still have 90% of the account and a clear head. Getting it wrong ten times in a row happens to everyone, sooner or later.

The R, a measure that doesn't lie

Instead of measuring results in euros, measure in R. One R is what you risk on a trade. If you risk 10 € and make 20 €, you've made 2R. If you lose the 10 €, you've lost 1R. R lets you compare trades of different sizes, and it takes the emotion out of the number.

TradeI riskedResultIn R
110 €+15 €+1.5R
210 €−10 €−1R
312 €+24 €+2R

Where to learn, without getting lost

There's far too much information. Pick one source, follow it to the end, and only then look for another. At MoreThanMoney you have:

  • "The Cold Method", the Forex book for beginners, with MetaTrader 5 step by step.
  • The video bootcamps for each strategy, free on YouTube (they're listed in "The MTM Scanners Guide").
  • The live classes and the community, to ask about anything you didn't understand.
Warning · Classic mistake · Starting on a live account "to take it seriously"

A live account doesn't make you more serious. It makes your mistakes more expensive. Make at least 30 trades on demo, with your plan, before you move to live.

Step 1 · The mental foundation

The market doesn't know you exist. So it isn't against you. You just have to stop working against yourself.

Everyone thinks the hard part of trading is the analysis. It isn't. The hard part is doing what you decided when the price is moving against you and your gut is telling you something else. That's why this first step ends here, in your head, not on the chart.

Gambler or investor

The gamblerThe investor
Wants excitementWants consistency
Measures themselves by the last tradeMeasures themselves by the month and the year
Increases the lot size to win it backKeeps the risk the same, win or lose
Decides during the tradeDecides beforehand, in writing
Hides the lossesLogs everything in the journal

Both use the same screens. Choose the right-hand column every day, especially on the days you feel like the left.

Your reason

Bad days will come. A run of losses, a week with no time, a friend telling you it's all a scam. On those days, the only thing holding you in place is knowing why you started.

Exercise · My reason

Write, in one sentence, why you want to put your money to work. Don't write "to get rich". Write what changes in your life.

The routine that fits into fifteen minutes

You don't need to spend all day staring at charts. In fact, people who spend all day looking tend to trade more and worse. A short routine, always the same, is enough.

  1. Context and calendar (3 min): is there any big news today? If so, take extra care.
  2. Reading with the scanner (5 min): what the tool says about your asset and your chart timeframe.
  3. Checklist and plan (4 min): have you met the rules? If not, there's no trade.
  4. Journal (3 min): record what you did and how you felt.

Don't do this alone

One of the most expensive mistakes I made was thinking I could do it alone. Having people to ask "does this make sense?" before clicking saves money. At MoreThanMoney the community exists for exactly that: questions answered by people who've been through them, live classes and rooms per strategy.

Exercise · To do today
  1. Choose a fixed time for your 15-minute routine: :
  2. Create a notebook or sheet for the journal, with these columns: date, asset, entry, stop, target, result in R, did I follow the plan?
  3. Join the community and introduce yourself in one line.

Step 2 · Choose how to take part

There's no single right way. There's the way that fits your life and that you can keep up.

With the first step done, you now know what risk, stop and R are, and you have a routine. Now you choose how you'll take part in the market. There are three ways, and each asks something different of you.

The three ways

WayWhat you doTime per dayFor whom
Trade with the toolsYou read the scanner, decide and execute15 to 30 minThose who want to learn the skill
Follow the house ideasYou get the idea with entry, stop and targets, and decide whether to enter5 to 15 minThose short on time who want to control each trade
Copy a strategyYou link your account and set the riskWeekly reviewThose who don't want to trade but want to follow along

Trade with the tools

MoreThanMoney's scanners mark trend, zones and signals on the TradingView chart and the house WebTrader. They don't decide for you. They save you time and help you avoid seeing things that aren't there. Each scanner has a free video bootcamp. If you want to start with one, "The MTM Scanners Guide" explains where to begin.

Follow the house ideas

The strategies' ideas reach your phone with everything marked: entry, stop and targets. With Tap to Trade, you open the trade with one tap on your account, once you've confirmed the volume. You're still the one deciding.

Illustrative screen.

Copy a strategy

With MTM Auto, your account at a regulated broker mirrors the trades of a house strategy. The money always stays in your account, in your name. Before copying, open the strategy's public audit and look at the full history, losses included. Past results do not guarantee future results.

Warning · Classic mistake · Picking the strategy that made the most last month

Last month is noise. Look at consecutive months, at the longest losing streak and at risk per trade. If you couldn't live through the strategy's worst phase, don't copy it.

4

Step 2 · Your first trade, with a cool head

A good trade is one that follows the plan. Win or lose.

Joana, 33, a designer in Lisbon, placed her first demo trade on a Thursday. It went wrong: the price hit the stop in twenty minutes. She was pleased. Not because she'd lost, but because she lost exactly what she'd decided to lose, not a cent more. For the first time, she felt she was in control of something.

The life of a trade

  1. Before: your routine tells you whether there's a trade. The checklist confirms it.
  2. Size: you calculate the volume from the stop, so you only risk your R.
  3. Entry: you open the order with the stop and target already set.
  4. Management: you let the rules work. You don't move the stop further away.
  5. After: you log it in the journal, with the result in R and your answer to "did I follow the plan?".

The right size, without complicated formulas

The most common mistake beginners make is always using the same lot size. The distance to the stop changes from trade to trade, so the same lot size risks different amounts. On the MoreThanMoney WebTrader you enter the risk as a percentage and the platform calculates the volume from the stop. In MetaTrader, do the maths with a calculator or with the table in "The Cold Method".

Losing streaks will happen

Even an approach that wins more often than it loses has losing streaks. It's not a sign that the method has stopped working. It's statistics. What protects you is small risk and the journal, which tells you after 30 trades whether the problem is the method or the execution.

Story · Joana, trade 12

Three losses in a row. On the fourth, the urge was to double the volume "to win it back". She opened her journal, saw the three losses had all followed the plan, and kept at 1%. The fourth hit the target. Doubling would have worked out too, but she'd have learned the wrong rule.

  2. Log it in the journal, with the result in R.
  3. Answer: did I follow the plan? ☐ yes ☐ no. If not, what did I change and why:
5

Step 3 · Automate

Automating isn't leaving things to chance. It's following rules without emotion.

After a few weeks on step 2, you'll notice something: the hard part isn't finding trades. It's managing the ones that are open. Moving the stop when price gets close, closing too early out of fear, forgetting to protect a trade that was already in profit. The third step exists to take those decisions out of your hands, in the moments when your hands are the problem.

What gets automated

WhatHowWhat it saves you from
ProtectionAuto Break-Even: the stop moves to entry when price reaches the first targetWatching a winning trade turn into a loss
FollowingTrailing Stop: the stop follows price at a fixed distanceClosing early out of fear
ExitsPartial exits at each targetHaving to decide everything at once
RecordHistory and journal togetherForgetting what you did and why
ProofA shareable auditRelying on screenshots

On the MoreThanMoney WebTrader, Auto Break-Even, Trailing Stop and partial exits run on the server, even with the tab closed. They work with demo accounts, MTM Funded accounts (simulated) and accounts with your own broker, on MetaTrader or TradeLocker.

Rules written down, not remembered

Automation starts on paper. Before you switch on any automation, write down the rules it's going to follow.

Exercise · My management rules
  • When it reaches the first target, I do: ☐ Break-Even ☐ partial exit ☐ both
  • Percentage I close at the first target: %
  • Trailing Stop: ☐ yes, at pips/points ☐ no
  • I stop trading for the day when I lose: R
  • I stop trading for the week when I lose: R
Key idea

The stop-trading rule is the most important automation of all. A bad day mustn't turn into a bad week.

The audit: your proof, for yourself

At the end of a month, open your history and your account's audit. Not to show anyone. To see, with numbers, whether you're sticking to the plan. The house accounts have public audits with every trade, and that's the standard I ask you to hold yourself to.

  2. Switch on Auto Break-Even on your demo account and make your next trade with it active.

Step 3 · Growing without greed

Grow slowly, based on results, not euphoria.

A good month always comes. And with it comes the temptation: double the capital, double the risk, open more assets. This is where many people hand back to the market everything they've learned. Growing is part of the plan, but it has rules, like everything else.

The scaling rule

Exercise · My scaling rule

I only increase the capital or the risk when

(Example: three months in a row of following the plan on at least 90% of trades, with the journal up to date.)

Notice that the rule is about following the plan, not about making money. One month of profit without following the plan is luck. Three months of following the plan is method.

Protect what you've built

  • Withdraw a part regularly. Freedom also means sleeping soundly.
  • Keep the emergency fund intact. Never use it to top up the trading account.
  • Review the plan every 30 days. Adjust based on the journal, not your mood.

The 30-day plan

2Step 2Choose the way and the asset, first 5 demo trades
